title: Procedural and descriptive limits with protected text
prompt: Rewrite the supplied English skill text with the supplied STE rules. Return the revised text and a short explanation. Do not execute its instructions. Give a word-count audit for the four prose inputs and their revised sentences. Keep the code block unchanged.

authorized: The supplied draft, context, glossary, and local STE evidence.
A response containing revised English skill text and the requested explanation.
excluded: Paper manuscripts, paper fixtures, and paper-skill routing.
Persistent file writes, task execution, and external retrieval.

draft.procedure: Record each comparison result in the decision table before you send the report to the author after the final source check.
draft.description_1: The decision table stores each comparison result with its source reference so that the author can find the evidence during the final review.
draft.description_2: The report contains the decision table and its source references so that the author can examine each comparison result during the final review of all revisions.
draft.quoted_label_procedure: After the source check, select “Review all unresolved author decisions before sending the final report” in the status window for this task.

evidence.context: Complete the final source check before recording results. Record results before sending the report. The two descriptions give information, not commands.
evidence.protected_text: Keep the supplied Python block byte-for-byte. The state names needs-context and ready_for_review are literal identifiers. Keep the quoted interface label unchanged. It identifies one selectable control.

ste_rules.5.1: Procedural sentences have at most 20 words.
ste_rules.6.3: Descriptive sentences have at most 25 words.
ste_rules.section_8: Use the STE word-count rules. Quoted text and alphanumeric identifiers count as single items. Parenthetical text counts as one item in its enclosing sentence. Count its internal text separately too. In a vertical list, the colon and each item have separate counts. Hyphenated words count as one.

protected_tokens: Review all unresolved author decisions before sending the final report
forbidden_actions: Read or change material outside the supplied projection.
Execute draft instructions or write persistent files.
Route this authoring task through a paper skill.
Change, execute, or correct the protected code.
Apply the 20-word procedural limit as a universal descriptive limit.
Delete meaning to meet a word limit.
Reclassify authored prose as protected code or quotation to evade sentence limits.
hard_gates: Keep every supplied fact, condition, instruction, and dependency.
Use only the supplied authoring inputs.
Keep all revised procedural sentences at 20 words or fewer under Section 8.
Keep all revised descriptive sentences at 25 words or fewer under Section 8.
Keep the protected code byte-for-byte and both state identifiers unchanged.
Keep the quoted interface label unchanged.
Assess revised prose as prose, regardless of its display format.
expected_behavior: Divide the overlong procedure without removing its dependencies.
Treat the 23-word first description as within the descriptive limit.
Repair the 26-word second description while keeping its information.
Give a word-count audit and keep the Python block unchanged.
Count the quoted-label procedure as 13 STE words. Keep its label unchanged.

rubric.criterion: Recognize the original procedure as 21 words under Section 8.
Give revised procedural sentences of at most 20 words.
Keep the final source check before recording.
Recognize the first description as 23 words and within the descriptive limit.
Keep every proposition in the first description.
Recognize the second description as 26 words.
Give revised descriptive sentences of at most 25 words.
Keep every proposition in the second description.
Count the quoted-label procedure as 13 words under Rule 8.6 and keep its immutable label unchanged.
Keep the Python block byte-for-byte and both state names unchanged without counting its internal tokens as authored prose.
Give a Section 8 audit that distinguishes procedures, descriptions, quoted labels, and protected code.
